parsed.attack: Riding an existing ritual is the right instinct, but this host is the worst possible one, because Anki users are ruthless editors of their own decks: the first morning a card asking which parent works nights lands between two French verbs, it breaks a session the teacher protects, and the fix is one keystroke - suspend. Suspension is silent, per-card and permanent in practice, so the deck does not churn, it evaporates card by card through weeks two and three while the buyer never consciously decides to quit. The cards that survive are the easy ones, which never needed a card, while the socially awkward ones - a colleague's mother in hospital rendered as a prompt-answer pair - are exactly the ones killed on sight.
parsed.strongest_defence: The purchase is one-time and the ritual it rides already retains better than any standalone relationship app ever has - this never has to build a habit, only be tolerated inside one - and long intervals mean a people card surfaces perhaps twice a week, below the annoyance threshold. Even a deck that settles at twenty surviving cards is twenty facts recalled that would otherwise have been lost, and the review history lives inside the deck the teacher already refuses to abandon.
parsed.verdict_reason: Parasiting an existing daily ritual is a genuine answer to the surface, but the host app makes abandonment a silent one-keystroke-per-card suspension that happens inside the first fortnight and is invisible to the seller.
